gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much each 120 V leg of these split-phase generators can carry: Honda's manual limits each of the EU7000iS's two circuits to 22.9 A (about 2,750 W) in 120/240 V mode. That is less per leg than the Champion 201417's 4,500 W, worked out from Champion's 37.5 A at 240 V, even though the Honda costs about twice as much.
standout_why: I compared four pages. Lights On Labs (cited) gives the EU7000iS only as 5,500/7,000 W with a '30 A, 125/250 V locking outlet' and does not cover split-phase, per-leg output or 240 V amps. Consumer Reports (cited) returned only navigation with no specs. homewelder.com gives 240 V running amps for other models (Champion 201175, Westinghouse iGen12000DFc, DuroMax XP11000iH) but says nothing on per-leg output and covers none of ChatGPT's five picks. rightgenerator.com lists receptacles and propane ratings but nothing on per-leg output, 240 V amps or split-phase. ChatGPT's own answer says a 50 A outlet does not mean 50 A at 240 V, so the outlet-versus-wattage point is already covered. The per-leg number, and the Honda voltage-selector rule that sets it, is not.
decides: This supports Champion 201417 as the pick for running a 120/240 V panel through a transfer switch or interlock. On gasoline it has the most capacity per leg among ChatGPT's five picks: 4,500 W, or about 4,044 W on propane. It also undercuts the Honda EU7000iS as the premium pick. In the 120/240 V position that a panel hookup needs, the Honda's per-leg limit is 22.9 A (about 2,748 W). Only the WEN DF680iX is lower, at 21.25 A (2,550 W). So a 120 V load that the Honda's 5,500 W rating suggests will run can trip one Honda circuit while the other has spare capacity. WEN TF1050iX is the best pick for anyone who will run on propane, because WEN rates it at the same 8,550 running watts on propane as on gasoline.

findings.label: Per-circuit (per-leg) limit in 120 V/240 V position
findings.value: 22.9 A per circuit (≈2,748 W at 120 V)
findings.source_title: Honda EU7000iS Owner's Manual, p.40 'Voltage Selector Switch' (ManualsLib copy)
findings.note: Manual: 'When the voltage selector switch is in the 120 V/240 V position, you must balance the load... each set of receptacles is powered by only one power producing circuit that can produce a maximum of 22.9 amps.' The two sets are receptacles 1, 3, 4B and receptacles 2, 4A. 22.9 A × 120 V = 2,748 W. Honda's US page returned 403, so this figure comes from the manual.

findings.label: 120 V total in 120 V ONLY position
findings.note: Manual: 'When the voltage selector switch is in the 120 V ONLY position, you do not need to spread the load over the receptacles' and the total load must not exceed 45.8 A. The same rated output therefore behaves differently depending on the switch position.

findings.note: Maker spec gives 240 V running current 37.5 A (gas) and 33.7 A (LPG), and 120 V running current 75 A total.
